title: 3D Surface Imaging After Breast Reduction Surgery
summary:
Background:
Three-dimensional (3D) surface imaging is gaining increasing importance in plastic surgery. This study evaluates a new software (VGG-SfM) based on the Structure-from-Motion approach with respect to its accuracy in digital breast surface assessment.

Methods:
In 40 female patients following reduction mammaplasty, the breast will be imaged three-dimensionally using both the Vectra H2 system and an iPhone 16 Pro Max in combination with the VGG-SfM software. Distances between anatomical landmarks will be measured, surface models compared, and two surgical techniques (T-scar and U-scar) analyzed based on anthropometric parameters.

This study aims at validating the VGG-SfM software for smartphone-based 3D surface imaging and to compare breast projection between the two surgical techniques.

interventions.name:
A total of 40 female patients who underwent reduction mammaplasty between June 2017 and July 2025 will be included in the study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Female patients who underwent reduction mammaplasty between June 2017 and July 2025, who have provided written informed consent to participate in the study, and who are of legal age.
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal to participate; allergy to adhesive markers; severe complications that significantly impede or prevent imaging; pregnancy or breastfeeding at the time of imaging.
